definitions.gloss: blatant lie; outright lie; barefaced lie
definitions.explanation: An obvious, complete falsehood with no truth whatsoever. The expression uses {真|ま}っ{赤|か} (bright red) metaphorically to mean 'complete' or 'utter.'

examples.japanese: それは{真|ま}っ{赤|か}な{嘘|うそ}だ。
{彼|かれ}の{言|い}い{訳|わけ}は{真|ま}っ{赤|か}な{嘘|うそ}だった。
examples.english: His excuse was a blatant lie.

examples.japanese: {真|ま}っ{赤|か}な{嘘|うそ}をついてまで{自分|じぶん}を{守|まも}ろうとするのはやめなさい。
examples.english: Stop trying to protect yourself by telling blatant lies.

notes:
USAGE:
A set expression meaning a complete, obvious lie. The {真|ま}っ{赤|か} here does not refer to the color red but is an intensifier meaning 'utter' or 'complete,' as in {真|ま}っ{赤|か}な{嘘|うそ}. This usage of {赤|あか} as an intensifier also appears in {真|ま}っ{赤|か}な{他人|たにん} (a complete stranger).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {真|ま}っ{赤|か}な{嘘|うそ}をつく (to tell a blatant lie)
- {真|ま}っ{赤|か}な{嘘|うそ}だと{見抜|みぬ}く (to see through a blatant lie)
